article_sentences: Cyclone Akvan Highlights: Cyclone Akvan has crossed the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coast close to Gopalpur by 8.30 am this (Friday) morning with much reduced wind speeds of 70-80 km/hr gusting to 90 km/hr, a few hours earlier than thought as it raced away to the coast at much higher speeds than the previous day.
The and fall process will continue into the net two hours, India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in a morning update.
The cyclone retained its status after having been flagged down two rungs from being a very severe cyclone earlier.
It had weakened after being caught in wedge between two ridges (high-pressure zones) and forced to wait for too long over the Bay if Bengal waters (see separate interview).

The IMD has forecast isolated heavy rainfall over south-east Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha, Jharkhand and Assam and Meghalaya tomorrow (Saturday) and over Chhattisgarh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura both today and tomorrow (Friday and Saturday) as Akvan makes the landfall and its remnant reaches inland.
It weakened into a deep depression after making landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha, is likely to bring heavy to very heavy rain across south Bengal till Saturday morning, the IMD said on Friday.

- November 20, 2026 15:40No major damage, loss of life in Odisha due to Cyclone Akvan: Minister (PTI)The India Meteorological Department (IMD), in a bulletin, said the landfall process started around 8 am and was completed by 11.20 am.
“Cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ crossed south coastal Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh close to Gopalpur with a wind speed of 70-80 kmph, gusting to 90 kmph between 7.30 am and 8.30 am.
The landfall process has completed,” the IMD said in its 11.20 am bulletin.
The cyclonic storm has weakened into a deep depression, with associated wind speed of 55-65 kmph gusting to 75 kmph over south coastal Odisha, the weather office said in its 1 pm bulletin.

The deep depression is likely to move north-northeastward and gradually weaken into a depression over the next six hours and into a well-marked low-pressure area in the subsequent six hours, it added.

stories.headline: Cauvery verdict is a reflection of the dire ground reality in Karnataka: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar
stories.title: Cauvery verdict is a reflection of the dire ground reality in Karnataka: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed a plea by Tamil Nadu claiming that Karnataka has to make good a shortfall of 16.01 tmcft (later modified to 11.719 tmcft) of Cauvery water on a pro rata basis during the current irrigation year of 2026-27.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Friday (November 20) described the Cauvery verdict as a reflection of the ground reality, adding that Karnataka would have supplied Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu if it had adequate reserves, but was currently struggling to meet even its own drinking water requirements.

The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed a plea by Tamil Nadu claiming that Karnataka has to make good a shortfall of 16.01 tmcft (later modified to 11.719 tmcft) of Cauvery water on a pro rata basis during the current irrigation year of 2026-27.

Tamil Nadu had accused its neighbouring State of withholding Cauvery water to the detriment of the inhabitants of Tamil Nadu, while Karnataka had pointed to the lack of a scientific formula for sharing distress in a pro rata or proportionate manner.
Mr. Shivakumar told reporters, “The order is only a reflection of the ground reality.
We don’t even have enough water for drinking purposes.
It is not as if we are holding back water that is available.
I have also told our farmers to be careful...
It is something that Tamil Nadu knows, we know and the whole world knows.
I could not even make an offering of bagina this year because of the dire water situation.”
Karnataka Water Resources Minister N. Cheluvarayaswamy said the verdict had come as a relief for the State.
“The verdict is to be seen more as justice to Karnataka rather than a setback to Tamil Nadu.
When we do not have adequate storage of water, how is it possible to release water to Tamil Nadu?” he asked.

stories.headline: Can't imagine how Sooryavanshi will destroy bowlers at 25: Ross Taylor
stories.title: Can't imagine how Sooryavanshi will destroy bowlers at 25: Ross Taylor
stories.summary: In his 16-year international career, Ross Taylor has notched up 93 half-centuries. But he is now chasing another—his 50th visit to India. “It’s my 49th time. One more and I will raise the bat,” says one of New Zealand’s most celebrated No. 3 batters. In India as an ambassador for the New Zealand pavilion at ProWine Mumbai 2026, an alcobev trade show, Taylor spoke to Forbes India about franchise cricket versus the rest, the growth of format specialists and the relevance of ODI cricket. Edited excerpts:It was nice to be the first to play 100 games in each format. Virat Kohli was the second one to do that. But with the way cricket's going and with franchise cricket, I think less and less players will be able to play all formats and more people will become 20-20 specialists. But I hope that people can still play the game of Test cricket, because that's the ultimate. But, also, 20-20 cricket's where the money is at and the fame for these younger players. Hopefully, in time, they will still want to play Test cricket.Q. So the format is going to consume the other formats of cricket?I think so, it’s almost doing that already.Q. Is it a good thing?No, I don’t think so. Because one-day cricket is still a great format to play. But, I think, out of the three formats, that's the one that's getting consumed by the amount of franchise cricket that's going on. I’m sure, in time, it will balance itself out, but maybe World Cups are where it's at for ODI cricket. We'll have to wait and see. Cricket is moving at a fast pace—when IPL started in 2008, I don’t think anyone could have envisioned it being as big and as popular as it is now.Q. Since you mentioned the ODI World Cup, the next one is just about a year away. The Indian team was recently in New Zealand to play an ODI series and you would have seen Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma in action. Do you see them making it to the next ODI World Cup?Without a doubt. Those were very tough conditions to play in New Zealand, but Rohit and Virat, the way they were fielding, was unbelievable. You wouldn't have thought that they were 38 and going on 40. I [not only] expect them to be in the team, but they'll also dominate. I think if they do win the Cup, that's Rohit and Kohli's finale—I think they'll retire from international cricket on a high. I hope for Indian fans and world cricket that they can at least get to a final with New Zealand and may the best team win.Q. You spoke about the growth of the IPL. The player that's got all of us talking since the last season is a 15-year-old: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who was recently in New Zealand for the T20 series. What's your assessment of his batting?Unbelievable, the fact that he's 15. My daughter's 15, and even she can’t believe it. And he's been doing it for so long as well. He started with Rajasthan Royals [RR] when he was 13. I watched video clips of him absolutely destroying bowlers in the nets. And you're thinking, he's only 15, what can he do when he's 25 and a fully grown man? At the moment, he's an amazing talent. And for Indian cricket, not only T20 cricket, I'm sure he's going to have a big future in both one-day and, hopefully, Tests as well.Q. How does he transition to a more patient approach with the red ball?At the end of the day, he just needs to play more cricket. Obviously, he's so successful in what he's doing at the moment. But once he has some more Ranji Trophy, some more [domestic cricket]... the world's ahead of him. It's really up to him whether he wants to change his game to play the longer format. But India loves its Test cricket just as much. And for him to be up there with Kohli and [Sachin] Tendulkar, [Rahul] Dravid and all the greats, he'll need to play Test cricket—and I'm sure he will in time. I’m sure we'll see his progress in the coming years.Q. He's also a very young player. How do you think his career needs to be managed?It's like anything else. You've still got to rely on your parents to guide you and make decisions for you. We saw how long a career Sachin Tendulkar had as a 16-year-old. And Sooryavanshi is even younger, so I hope he is managed well.I know Shane Bond, the bowling coach at RR, very well. He says he's a great kid. And he keeps learning and maturing every year that he's down with him. So I think it's going to be an exciting time for him. Like any cricketer, he’s going to go through ups and downs. But it's exciting to see where he can get to and how he can transform the sport.Q. He's become the captain of his state team in the domestic T20 league. Do you think it's too early or he's going to mature into the role?As I said, he's going to mature naturally in his own time. But the coaching staff and management obviously see him as a leader and having that extra responsibility, I think it's great to give it to him early on. It just sounds strange when you're talking about a 15-year-old. But he's an exciting talent. I'm sure captaincy will bring out a different side to him. And he'll learn a lot, and will put his own style on the role as well.Q. You're here at ProWine 2026 as the ambassador for New Zealand wines. You have your own wine line as well. You’ve also played T20 cricket for Samoa last year. There’s lots going on post retirement.When people ask me what I'm doing, I feel like I'm not doing a lot, but then when you pull the layers back, I'm very busy. It's great to be in India. It's my 49th time in India—one more and then I'll raise the bat [laughs].We hosted Prime Minister Narendra Modi in July this year, and it was nice to get the free trade agreement across the line. It’s also nice to bring my own wine label that is selling in New Zealand to India and hopefully fans of cricket can try the wine and enjoy it.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves additional ₹5 crore for Afzalpur Praja Soudha building, says Priyank Kharge
stories.title: Cabinet approves additional ₹5 crore for Afzalpur Praja Soudha building, says Priyank Kharge
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The State Cabinet has approved an additional grant of ₹5 crore to complete the second phase of construction of the Taluk Praja Soudha building at Afzalpur in Kalaburagi district, Minister for Home, IT&BT and Kalaburagi district in-charge.
Priyank Kharge said.
In a media note released on Friday, Mr. Kharge said that additional funding was required to complete the construction of the second and third floors.
“The government had accorded administrative approval on January 25, 2022, for the construction of the building at an estimated cost of ₹10 crore.
The project was taken up with the objective of bringing various government offices under one roof and enabling people to access different public services at a single location,” Mr. Kharge said.
With the Cabinet’s approval of the additional ₹5 crore, the total estimated cost of the project would increase to ₹15 crore, including the earlier sanctioned amount of ₹10 crore, he added.
The Taulk Praja Soudha was expected to make it easier and quicker for people to access services offered by various government departments.

It would also reduce the need for residents, particularly those from rural areas, to travel to different offices for official work and was expected to improve administrative efficiency at the taluk level, Mr. Kharge noted.

Strengthening infrastructure essential for the overall development of Kalaburagi district remains a priority, Mr. Kharge said, adding that the government was committed to making public services more accessible and citizen-friendly by providing better administrative facilities at the taluk level.

stories.headline: 'Shocking The Conscience' Not Enough To Modify Arbitral Award: Supreme Court Restores Contractor's Claim Against Kolkata Port Trust
stories.title: 'Shocking The Conscience' Not Enough To Modify Arbitral Award: Supreme Court Restores Contractor's Claim Against Kolkata Port Trust
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has set aside a Calcutta High Court judgment that reduced an arbitral award in favour of a dredging contractor by 50%, holding that a court exercising jurisdiction under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, cannot interfere with an award merely because the amount granted for additional work appears excessive.

The Court held that the High Court's conclusion that the claim for additional work, which exceeded 70% of the original contract value, shocked its conscience was not a legally sustainable ground for modifying the award.

A bench of Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice K. Vinod Chandran set aside a Calcutta High Court Division Bench order that had reduced the arbitral award by 50% on the ground that the amount awarded for additional work exceeded the original contract value by over 70%.

The Court noted that since the additional amount arose from repeated dredging undertaken by the contractor to keep the channel and basin operational, thus, the High Court had mechanically exercised its jurisdiction under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, to set aside the award on the mere ground that it exceeded the contract work value merely noting that it shocked the court's conscience without providing a “substantive reason which blatantly and patently brings forth the conflict with the most basic notions of morality or justice, resulting in the conscience of the Court being shocked.”

“…the impugned order has merely used the words on the sole ground of the bills for the additional work having exceeded 70% of the original contract; without looking at the nature of the additional work involved… The Division Bench considering the application under Section 37 has not looked into the measurement or the invoices, which in any event, would be an exercise of adjudication on merits, clearly prohibited under the Act of 1996.
The measurements and invoices raised are of one character, based on the additional work of redredging which cannot be compartmentalised as 'valid' and 'invalid'.”, the Court said.

The dispute arose from a contract awarded by the Kolkata Port Trust to Marino Dredgeco for dredging the riverbed and shores at Sagar Island to create an approach channel and basin for a pilot station.
During execution, repeated dredging became necessary due to siltation, adverse weather conditions, and differences between the actual soil conditions and the data supplied by the Port Trust.
The Port Trust also entrusted additional work through a letter dated July 19, 2000.
After completing the work, the contractor raised additional bills, which led to arbitration.
The Arbitrator awarded the claimed amounts, and the Single Judge upheld the award under Section 34.

However, the High Court Division Bench, in an appeal under Section 37, reduced the amount by 50% and reduced interest, reasoning that the additional-work claims exceeded 70% of the original contract value and shocked the Court's conscience, following which an appeal was filed by the award holder, Marino Dredgeco, before the Supreme Court.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Rejects Plea Seeking Maintenance Of Police Database On Persons Making Repeated Sexual Offense Complaints
stories.title: Supreme Court Rejects Plea Seeking Maintenance Of Police Database On Persons Making Repeated Sexual Offense Complaints
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today refused to entertain a plea seeking a structured database of complainants who lodge multiple sexual-offence cases.
Underlining the need to protect identity of victims/complainants, as well as referring to existing identification mechanisms, the Court dismissed the plea.
A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was dealing with a challenge to the Delhi High Court order which disposed of the petitioner's PIL seeking similar relief.
The High Court had directed the Delhi.
Police and other authorities to expeditiously decide the petitioner's representation seeking such a database.
During the hearing, the petitioner's counsel urged that the petitioner was seeking such a database at police headquarters in every district.
Justice Bagchi remarked that such a database could serve as a "gateway to the disclosure of identity (of victims)".

The judge further noted that a 2-layer identification mechanism is already in place for sexual offense cases, as (i) the law requires medical examination of a victim (including DNA profiling), (ii) the statement of a victim is recorded before a Magistrate.
"The law itself provides for lawyers of privacy for the victims.
You want this to be maintained with the police station, which in our considered opinion is a gateway of disclosure of identity.
The concern that you are expressing - that a person masquerades and makes false complaints in a serial manner can be restricted if there is a database.
With regard to identity, in respect of sexual offenses, there is no difficulty.

stories.headline: Supreme Court allows lighting of lamp on ‘Deepathoon’ at Thirupparankundram as limited one-time arrangement
stories.title: Supreme Court allows lighting of lamp on ‘Deepathoon’ at Thirupparankundram as limited one-time arrangement
stories.summary: A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar however stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras HC in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the ‘Deepathoon’ as an essential practice
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) allowed the lighting of the lamp, as a “limited one-time arrangement”, on the ‘Deepathoon’ at the Thirupparankundram Hill on Karthigai Deepam day (November 24, 2026).

A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, however, stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras High Court in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the ‘Deepathoon’ as an essential practice.
The court issued notice on the appeals filed by the State.

The interim order dealt with pleas by the State to stay the January 6 judgment and also looked into the question whether the lamp could be lit on the ‘Deepathoon’ on the forthcoming Karthigai Deepam festival day falling on November 24.

Pronouncing the interim order, Justice Kumar said the court was aware of the dangers of allowing once becoming a precedent, while also noting that two separate Benches of the High Court had allowed the lighting of the lamp.
Imposing restrictions and safeguards, the Supreme Court directed that the Devasthanam would exclusively decide the members of the team to light the lamp on November 24.
The Madurai District Collector would act as nodal officer for the event.
The Commissioner of Madurai.
Police has to provide the ring of security.
The Centre was directed to supplement security arrangements with CRPF personnel, if required.
No procession, slogan-raising or permission to gathering of general public will be allowed, the court directed.
The access to lamp-lighting would be allowed to only authorised persons.

stories.headline: Arunachal Congress urges Centre not to impose Siang dam project on indigenous communities
stories.title: Arunachal Congress urges Centre not to impose Siang dam project on indigenous communities
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah is expected to discuss national security and infrastructure development during his three-day tour of Arunachal Pradesh
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'national security' in summary weight 42
article_sentences: Hours before Union Home Minister Amit Shah began his three-day tour of Arunachal Pradesh on Friday (November 20, 2026), the Congress asked him if the Centre would give a written assurance that it would not “impose” the 11,000-megawatt Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) on the State’s indigenous communities.
Mr. Shah is expected to discuss national security and infrastructure development during his visit.
The Centre proposed SUMP as a counter to a 60,000-MW hydropower project that China is building upstream across the Yarlung Zangbo in the Tibet region.
Violent protests had erupted against the project due to fears that it would displace or affect more than 1.25 lakh people, mostly from the Adi community.

In a statement issued late on Thursday evening (November 19, 2026), the Arunachal Pradesh unit of the Congress said development without transparency and governance without accountability cannot deliver sustainable progress.

The party said communities likely to be affected by SUMP had raised serious concerns regarding ancestral land, displacement, environmental and geological risks, livelihoods, cultural heritage and the future of indigenous institutions.
“The continuing protests and the reported deployment of security personnel have further heightened tensions in the Siang region,” it said.
The Congress asked Mr. Shah to specify whether the Centre would give a written assurance that SUMP would not be imposed against the wishes of the indigenous communities.
“Will the Centre direct the suspension of disputed pre-feasibility report activities until meaningful consultations, legally required procedures, and independent assessments are completed?
Why should indigenous people face the presence of extensive security personnel when they are raising legitimate concerns through democratic protests?” the Congress asked.

The party also asked whether Mr. Shah would meet representatives of the Siang Indigenous Farmers’ Forum (SIFF), villagers likely to be affected, indigenous organisations and civil society representatives.

“Of particular concern is the reported request by SIFF for an appointment with the Union Home Minister during his visit, which, according to media reports, has not been accommodated in the announced itinerary.
